episodes.title: Introduction to Biology
episodes.description: You’ll learn how all of life is connected, and why studying biology can help us better understand ourselves and our relationship to all living things.

episodes.title: The Scientific Method
episodes.description: Science offers a way of discovering and understanding the world around us, driven by questions and tested with evidence.

episodes.title: What Biologists Do
episodes.description: Explore how biologists investigate life, including their use of model organisms such as zebrafish and fruit flies.

episodes.title: How Life is Organized
episodes.description: We’ll uncover the levels of biological organization, discover soil’s superpowers, and find out why the biosphere is kind of like a really, really long train.

episodes.title: Intro to Ecology: Why Did All These Elephants Die?
episodes.description: Ecology is the study of the interactions of living things with each other and their environment.

episodes.title: Community Ecology: Interspecies Interactions
episodes.description: Explore predator-prey relationships, parasitism, mutual benefits, keystone species, and the recovery of disrupted ecological communities.

episodes.title: Population Ecology
episodes.description: We’ll take a look at the methods population ecologists use to study a population and the types of data they collect.

episodes.title: What is Climate Change?
episodes.description: Explore the greenhouse effect, the science of climate change, and how today's warming differs from changes in Earth's past.

episodes.title: The Effects of Climate Change
episodes.description: Climate change shakes up all of Earth’s systems, including the living ones.

episodes.title: Conservation Biology: Sixth Mass Extinction?
episodes.description: Explore how conservation biology protects biodiversity and restores habitats, including the return of wolves to Yellowstone.

episodes.title: Intro to Evolution: What We Can Learn From a Giraffe’s Neck
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Biology, we’ll learn how evolution explains life’s unity and its diversity.

episodes.title: Microevolution: What’s An Allele Got to Do With It?
episodes.description: We’ll learn about the Hardy-Weinberg equation, how your alleles make you uniquely you, and how some tigers changed their stripes.

episodes.title: Natural Selection: Life’s way of Stayin’ Alive
episodes.description: Explore how natural selection shapes traits, with examples ranging from ginkgo trees to hurricane-surviving lizards.

episodes.title: Population Genetics: Why Do We Have Different Skin Colors?
episodes.description: Compare genetic variation within populations to understand evolution, human diversity, and the limitations of biological ideas about race.

episodes.title: Speciation: Where Do Species Come From?
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Biology, we’ll learn about speciation—a process that can happen over millions of years, or within a single generation.

episodes.title: Evolutionary History: The Timeline of Life
episodes.description: Trace the history of life on Earth through major evolutionary changes and periods of diversification.

episodes.title: Phylogeny: How We’re All Related
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Biology, we’ll learn why this kingdom-phylum stuff is going out of style and why phylogenetic trees are in.

episodes.title: Biological Diversity, Butts, and the Tree of Life
episodes.description: Explore the Tree of Life and how evolutionary relationships connect Earth's diverse organisms, including humans.

episodes.title: Human Evolution: We Didn’t Evolve From Chimps
episodes.description: Trace human evolution and meet the close relatives that help explain our species’ origins.

episodes.title: Carbon & Biological Molecules: What is Life Made Of?
episodes.description: Explore the building blocks of major biological molecules and how they combine into the macromolecules that make up living things.

episodes.title: The Unexpected Truth About Water
episodes.description: In this Episode of Crash Course Biology, we’ll learn about how water’s polarity and hydrogen bonding helps it sustain life on a larger scale.

episodes.title: Microscopes: How We See What We Can’t See
episodes.description: Compare major microscope types and learn how scientists use light microscopes to investigate tiny structures.

episodes.title: A Tour of the Cell
episodes.description: Compare prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, tour a eukaryotic cell, and explore its origins through endosymbiosis.

episodes.title: Cell Membranes: How Does Stuff Get Into Your Cells?
episodes.description: The cell membrane is a protein-studded phospholipid bilayer that not only protects our cells, but also regulates what goes in and out.

episodes.title: Why Do Cells Need to Communicate?
episodes.description: We’ll learn that our cells are in constant communication, reminding each other—and themselves—to perform important functions like breathing, walking, or even sleeping.

episodes.title: Chemical Reactions in Biology
episodes.description: We’ll learn how our cells use energy, what an enzyme’s role is in chemical reactions, and what makes a reaction exergonic or endergonic.

episodes.title: Cellular Respiration: Do Cells Breathe?
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Biology, we’re taking a deep dive into cellular respiration, the process that produces the ATP inside of our mitochondria.

episodes.title: Photosynthesis: The Original Solar Power
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Biology, we’ll explore photosynthesis in two acts, and learn how the process works inside and out.

episodes.title: Mitosis & the Cell Cycle: How Cells Clone Themselves
episodes.description: Follow a cell’s life cycle through mitosis, including how division is regulated and what happens when regulation fails.

episodes.title: Meiosis: Why Are All Humans Unique?
episodes.description: We’ll discover how egg and sperm cells get made and learn why you’re a totally unique remix of your parents’ DNA.

episodes.title: Intro to Genetics: Why Your Cat Looks Like That
episodes.description: Explore basic inheritance patterns and how genes influence traits such as cat fur.

episodes.title: Genetic Traits: Nature? Nurture? Not That Simple
episodes.description: Discover how interactions between genes and environmental conditions shape traits in humans and other organisms.

episodes.title: DNA Structure & Replication: Our Instruction Manual for Existing
episodes.description: Explore DNA's molecular structure and how cells copy genetic instructions through replication.

episodes.title: Transcription: How mRNA Helped Save Lives
episodes.description: We learn about the role of messenger RNA in living things and how it decodes our DNA instruction manual through transcription.

episodes.title: Translation: How RNA Gets Translated into Protein Power
episodes.description: We’ll cover codon-reading ribosomes, tRNA delivery trucks, and scientists who are using what they know about translation to save lives.

episodes.title: How Genes Express Themselves
episodes.description: Explore how gene expression is regulated and how cells with shared DNA develop different functions and respond to their environment.

episodes.title: Genetic Mutations: Is Drinking Milk a Super Power?
episodes.description: Explore genetic mutations, including substitutions and frameshifts, and how CRISPR/Cas9 and gene therapy can modify genetic information.

episodes.title: Bacterial DNA & Genetics
episodes.description: In this episode, we’ll explore what bacteria are doing with their DNA — including how they can trade it around.

episodes.title: Viruses & Vaccines: How Do Vaccines Work?
episodes.description: In today’s episode of Crash Course Biology, we’ll learn why viruses are like genes in a box, and how they invade and spread between cells.

episodes.title: Bioinformatics: How Data Saves Lives
episodes.description: We’ll learn what bioinformatics is, how it works, and how scientists have used it to better understand everything from evolution to a viral epidemic.

episodes.title: Multicellular Function: Why We Aren’t Just One Big Cell
episodes.description: Explore how multicellular organisms are organized, maintain homeostasis, and develop complex forms.

episodes.title: Plant Anatomy & Physiology: Plants Are Hardcore
episodes.description: In this episode, we’ll learn how plants get resources, get rid of waste, stay defended, govern themselves, and much more.

episodes.title: How Animals Turn Resources Into Waste: The Poop Episode
episodes.description: Explore the respiratory, digestive, and urinary systems and compare how animals acquire resources and eliminate waste.

episodes.title: Animal Infrastructure: Why You’re More Than Goo
episodes.description: We’ll tour the cardiovascular, lymphatic, and musculoskeletal systems, learning how all of them keep a vertebrate’s inner workings connected, powered up, and ready to move.

episodes.title: Animal Defense Systems: How Skin, Snot, and Cells Keep Us Healthy
episodes.description: Explore animal immune defenses, from skin and inflammation to adaptive immune cells and antibodies.

episodes.title: Nervous & Endocrine Systems: What Really Happens When You Step on a Lego
episodes.description: Explore how the nervous and endocrine systems use neurons and hormones to coordinate animal bodies.

episodes.title: Sexual & Asexual Reproduction: How Animals Do It
episodes.description: In this episode, we’ll learn about sexual and asexual reproduction, internal and external fertilization, and all the ways that life, uh… finds a way.

episodes.title: Gender, Sex, & Sexuality: What’s the Difference?
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Biology, we’ll discover sex and sexuality as a continuum across life.

episodes.title: Animal Behavior: Why This Toad Is Bad at Jumping
episodes.description: Explore how scientists study the immediate and evolutionary causes of animal behavior, including animal decision-making.

episodes.title: Biology and You: The Dr. Sammy Show
episodes.description: Dr. Sammy answers audience questions and shows how biology can illuminate everyday experiences and help solve problems.
